partners.mechanism_chain: CFTR (HGNC:2408) —DISRUPTS→ protein folding and quality control (GO:0006457); protein folding and quality control (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Cystic fibrosis (MONDO:0009061); PSMC3 (HGNC:9123) —DISRUPTS→ proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508); proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Ebstein-Bezieau neurodevelopmental syndrome (MONDO:0981163); protein folding and quality control (GO:0006457) —BINDS→ proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508). Mutations in CFTR disrupt protein folding and quality control pathways (GO:0006457), leading to cystic fibrosis. Concurrently, mutations in PSMC3, a subunit of the 26S proteasome, disrupt proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508), leading to Ebstein-Bezieau neurodevelopmental syndrome. Both protein folding/quality control and proteasomal degradation are critical components of cellular proteostasis, thus representing a convergence at the level of cellular proteostasis.

partners.mechanism_chain: CFTR (HGNC:2408) —DISRUPTS→ epithelial ion and fluid transport (GO:0007049); epithelial ion and fluid transport (GO:0007049) —LEADS_TO→ abnormal mucus (HP:0002087); ABCB4 (HGNC:2408) —DISRUPTS→ bile acid transport (GO:0019754); bile acid transport (GO:0019754) —LEADS_TO→ gallstones (HP:0002128); bile acid transport (GO:0019754) —LEADS_TO→ cholestasis (HP:00114377); epithelial ion and fluid transport (GO:0007049) —BINDS→ bile acid transport (GO:0019754). Loss-of-function mutations in CFTR disrupt epithelial ion and fluid transport, leading to abnormal mucus, which can secondarily affect biliary epithelium. Loss-of-function mutations in ABCB4 disrupt bile acid transport by impairing phospholipid secretion, leading to gallstones and cholestasis. The disruption of epithelial barrier function and fluid homeostasis in cystic fibrosis can indirectly impact bile composition and flow, converging with the direct disruption of bile acid transport in gallbladder disease.

#### 1. deafness, cataract, impaired intellectual development, and polyneuropathy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.513)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-382556, Reactome:R-HSA-5678895, Reactome:R-HSA-5689880)

**Proposed mechanism:** CFTR (HGNC:2409) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272); Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272) —LEADS_TO→ proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0000422); PSMC3 (HGNC:9777) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272); Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272) —LEADS_TO→ proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0000422); Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272) —LEADS_TO→ Deafness (HP:0000365); Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272) —LEADS_TO→ Cataract (HP:0000501); Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired intellectual development (HP:0001249); Abnormal intracellular protein folding (HP:0011272) —LEADS_TO→ Polyneuropathy (HP:0003489). Loss-of-function mutations in CFTR lead to abnormal intracellular protein folding, which in turn disrupts proteasome-mediated protein degradation. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PSMC3 directly disrupt the proteasome, leading to abnormal intracellular protein folding and the associated phenotypes of deafness, cataract, impaired intellectual development, and polyneuropathy.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of proteasomal dysfunction in cystic fibrosis and the PSMC3-related syndrome could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both conditions, potentially involving proteasome modulators or strategies to enhance protein clearance.
